subtitle: Lesson 20 · Zero Trust for Data and Applications

eyebrow: Every earlier assumption breaks at once

steps.label: Vendor hosts it
steps.sub: no network path for your enforcement points to intercept

steps.label: Shadow IT
steps.sub: adopted without IT provisioning or visibility

steps.label: Discovery first
steps.sub: you can't govern an app nobody registered

eyebrow: CASB — sits between users and the SaaS app
code:
user --> [ CASB: proxy or API ] --> SaaS app

if file.label == "Restricted"
  AND app NOT sanctioned:
    block_upload()
if signin.risk == high:
    require_step_up_mfa()
caption: A CASB extends DLP and conditional access to apps you don't host the infrastructure of.

eyebrow: SSPM — checks the app's own configuration
code:
scan SaaS_tenant.settings:
  - public sharing links left open?
  - admin accounts without MFA?
  - default role over-permissive?
  - OAuth app granted excess scope?
// a CASB on the traffic path never sees these
caption: Misconfigurations inside the vendor's platform, not traffic — the SaaS equivalent of a posture scan.

eyebrow: Your identity provider still sits in the path

steps.label: Federated sign-in
steps.sub: SaaS auth routes through your own identity provider

steps.label: Same policy
steps.sub: MFA, device compliance, location checks still apply

steps.label: OAuth consent
steps.sub: govern & audit every 'Allow' click, not just sign-in
